name: relative energies of the closed-shell C1H2O2 isomers (formic acid vs dioxirane)

prompt.query: Determine the relative energies of the two closed-shell C1H2O2 isomers: formic acid and dioxirane. Species SMILES: C(=O)O; target SMILES: C1OO1; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: gas phase. Within the allowed methods, model the system so that it approximates the real conditions stated above as closely as the level of theory permits. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [CH:1](=[O:2])[O:3][H:4]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). Model the process you investigate as a graph and maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root: nodes for every species or electronic state you characterize (with SMILES) and edges for the state changes or transformations between them (with `via` pointing to the TS node id when a transition state was located). Use exactly this JSON shape (key names matter: nodes carry `id`, `role` (one of reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state) and `smiles` (a list of SMILES strings), and may optionally carry a `properties` object for declared quantities; edges carry `id`, `from`, `to`, `via`, `bond_changes` and optionally `barrier_kcal_mol`, `channel` and `favored`): {"nodes": [{"id": "RC", "role": "reactant", "smiles": ["..."]}, {"id": "TS1", "role": "transition_state", "smiles": []}, {"id": "P", "role": "product", "smiles": ["..."]}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "RC", "to": "P", "via": "TS1", "bond_changes": {"break": [[1, 2]], "form": [[1, 5]]}, "barrier_kcal_mol": 21.3}]}. Extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every state you actually characterized. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or state-change step carries two empty lists. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Declare the energy difference in kcal/mol between dioxirane and formic acid (state which isomer is the global minimum) as a structured `properties` object on the target-state (product) node in mechanism_graph.json, using these unit-carrying keys: `energy_relative_to_reactant_kcal_mol`, `state_ordering`. String values are allowed for descriptive entries. `state_ordering` states which state lies lower (e.g. "<species A> below <species B>"). If a particular species or transition state cannot be computed to a trustworthy accuracy with the allowed methods, mark the corresponding node or edge "accessible": false in mechanism_graph.json and deliver the rest of the graph as usual; the graph still starts at the reactant complex. The scorer reads that structured flag, not prose; do not declare a number you cannot stand behind. Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.
